transcription: CEDAS has entered Customs and the next step is to prepare a Mexican Customs entry. In Mexico we call them Pedimentos. It's really an appraisal sheet. It's a breakdown of the sheet. Usually the same information. That's right. But here you give them all the information. For example, let me see if I've got one right here. You give them all the information on... on what the invoice contains. There's one. On what the invoice contains. What the material is. It's all physically here. For example, this is some bottling equipment going over there. And on this appraisal sheet you tell them who it's for. Who made the invoice out of the States. This came from St. Louis, Missouri. How much the freight was. And on the reverse of this thing, you put that everything has to be marked. In other words, this identification number is that traffic number I spoke to you a little while ago. Number of boxes, what they contain, the tariff duty, the tariff number, the ad valorem rate, and what the actual duties would be paid. For example, here it would be 996 pesos and 73 cents. As you can see, this is a form that has already been approved by the appraiser. These appraisers are called vistas. It's very different from the vistas we have nowadays.
